texts.facts: - 1. This is an ordinary suit for recovery of principal amount of Rs. 8,99,600/- with pendente-lite and future interest and costs. 2. The plaintiff no. 1 is the Insurance Company incorporated and registered under the Indian Companies Act, 1956. The plaintiff no. 2 had consigned basmati rice bags to defendant for transportation after getting the same insured with plaintiff no. 1. The defendant is a common carrier within the meaning of Carriage by Road Act, 2007. The plaintiff no. 2 booked the consignment of basmati rice vide invoice no. 3298, dated 30.08.2018 of total price of Rs. 16,61,489/- vide GR No. 2742, dated 30.08.2018, comprising of 840 bags, with defendant for transporting from Delhi to Secunderabad, Telangana and the defendant had undertaken to transport it in safe and sound condition for valuable consideration. While transporting, the driver of truck no. HR-73- 6386 stopped the truck in between Gwalior and Jhansi on 01.09.2018 for getting the truck repaired urgently. Suddenly, the CS (COMM) No.: 592/22 National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Delhi M. P. Freight Carrier Digitally signed by UMED UMED Date: SINGH SINGH 2025.03.04 16:56:11 +0530 ~3~ heavy rain started and after stoppage of the same, the driver started onward journey and reached destination on 04.09.2018. It was found while unloading the goods that a lot of water had entered in the body of the truck due to use of old tarpaulin cover. G. I. Sheet was not used to cover the body of the truck due to which the water entered in the basmati rice bags damaging them. The consignment was damaged due to the negligence of the carrier and same amounts to breach of the duty and so notice dated 07.09.2018 was sent to defendant under Section 16 of Carriage by Road Act, by plaintiff no. 2 asking it to pay damages for loss to consignment of 617 bags of basmati rice, each of 25 kg, @ Rs. 7,900/- per quintal totaling to Rs. 12,18,575/- . In turn, the defendant also acknowledged loss caused to plaintiff no. 2 and issued Damage Certificate dated 07.09.2018. The plaintiff no. 2, having been insured by plaintiff no. 1 from 13.01.2018 to 12.01.2019, intimated plaintiff no. 1 regarding damages pursuant to which surveyor National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Delhi M P Freight Carrier on 4 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44718677/ 2 namely T. Rama Gopal was appointed to assess loss and he filed report on 07.10.2018 assessing loss to the tune of Rs. 6,97,364/-. After receipt of the report, the plaintiff no. 1 scrutinized the claim as per contractual obligations and settled the dispute with plaintiff no. 2 for Rs. 6,97,364/- and thereafter, plaintiff no. 2 subrogated all its rights and claims in the subject matter in favour of plaintiff no. 1 by executing subrogation letter and SPA. The defendant caused a loss of Rs. 6,97,364/- to plaintiff no. 2 who has given CS (COMM) No.: 592/22 National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Delhi M. P. Freight Carrier Digitally signed by UMED UMED Date: SINGH SINGH 2025.03.04 16:56:18 +0530 ~4~ subrogation letter to plaintiff no. 1 and hence the plaintiff no. 1 is entitled to that amount from defendant with interest @ 12% from 01.02.2019 to 30.06.2021 i.e. for 29 months, which comes out to Rs. 2,02,236/-. So the total claim amount is Rs. 8,99,600/-. 3. Despite service, no one appeared on behalf of defendant nor written statement was filed and hence defence was struck off and following notional issues were framed on 01.02.2021 :- 1. Learned counsel for plaintiffs argued that defendant is a reputed and experienced carrier and it should have taken proper care for the safety of the consignment but it acted negligently and did not use G. I. sheet to cover the body of the truck. Due to use of old tarpauline cover, the heavy rain water entered in the body resulting into entry of water in the basmati rise bags due to which the packets were damaged. Even the defendant had admitted loss in damage report. The Surveyor appointed by plaintiff no. 1 quantified the lost as Rs. 6,97,334/- which has already been paid by plaintiff no. 1 to plaintiff no. 2 who, after receipt of money, executed subrogation letter and SPA in favour of plaintiff no. 1 for recovery of that amount with damages. 6. Ex. PW1/8 is policy no. 401900211710000039 vide which the plaintiff no. 2 got his goods insured from plaintiff no. 1 for one year from 13.01.2018 to 12.01.2019 by paying a total premium of Rs. 94,401/-. The amount of sum assured was Rs. two crores and it is clearly mentioned in the policy that the CS (COMM) No.: 592/22 National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Delhi M. P. Freight Carrier Digitally signed by UMED UMED Date: SINGH SINGH 2025.03.04 16:56:31 +0530 ~6~ commodity was rice and paddy of all kinds. Thereafter, the plaintiff no. 2 prepared invoice Ex. PW1/3, dated 30.08.2018 of 840 bags of basmati rice each of 25 kg totalling to Rs. 16,61,489/-. The rice was to be transported to Sh. Ganpati Sales Corporation Secunderabad, Telangana. The goods were entrusted to defendant vide E-Way bill generated on 30.08.2018 and goods receipt Ex. PW1/4. But the rice was spoiled by rain water and hence, the plaintiff no. 2 issued notice Ex. PW1//5, dated 07.09.2018 to defendant intimating it for the loss and also claiming damages. After receipt of notice, the defendant also got the matter investigated and came to the conclusion that loss amount was Rs. 7,61,407/- sent report Ex. PW1/7, dated 07.09.2018 to plaintiff no. 2. After intimation, the plaintiff no. 1 also got surveyed the matter through T. Rama Gopal who furnished report dated 07.10.2018 Ex. PW1/9 to the effect that on receipt of communication on 04.09.2018 from the Hyderabad office of the plaintiff no. 1, he reached consignee's premises and noticed leakage of rain water in the backyard of the truck i.e. in the portion behind the driver seat. Due to pilferage of water, the basmati rise bags were found damaged and hence he advised the consignee to unload the truck and segregate the damaged goods. Complete stock of 840 bags was unloaded on 05.09.2018 and damaged goods were separated and on verification, he found that 223 bags were in undamaged condition but 617 bags were wet CS ( COMM ) No.: 592/22 National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Delhi M. P. Freight Carrier Digitally signed by UMED UMED SINGH SINGH Date: 2025.03.04 16:56:37 +0530 ~7~ and they were kept separately. It is next mentioned in the report that the old tarpauline cover could not stop entry of rain water in the body of the truck and hence, the basmati rice bags were spoiled. It is next mentioned that 617 bags containing basmati rice each of 25 kg were sold by the consignee @ Rs. 33 per kg, totaling Rs. 5,09,025/- due to which some loss was lessened. Ultimately, he came to the conclusion that after deducting sale price of spoiled goods totaling to National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Delhi M P Freight Carrier on 4 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44718677/ 4 Rs. 5,09,025/-, the total loss was Rs. 6,97,364/- after giving discount of 1% of the consignment value. After receipt of surveyor's report, the plaintiff no. 1 paid an amount of Rs. 6,97,364/- to plaintiff no. 2 on 24.01.2019 vide receipt Ex. PW1/10 and only thereafter, the plaintiff no. 2 issued subrogation letter and SPA in favour of plaintiff no. 1 pursuant to which the suit was filed. 7. The above discussion shows that due to the negligent act of the common carrier i.e. defendant, a loss of Rs. 6,97,364/- was caused to plaintiff no. 2 who had got the consignment insured from plaintiff no. 1. So, plaintiff no. 1 had to pay that much loss to plaintiff no. 2. 8.
